newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on soybean drop, fund sales.

text.p: A drop in the soybean market plus end of the month fund selling, tied to long liquidation, pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.

"End of the month fund profit taking," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International referring to the slide in soy, corn and wheat futures prices. "They've been buying it all month and don't want to hold it."
Weather outlooks received mixed reviews with warm temperatures seen boosting crop development but with some concerns about outlooks for dry weather over the near term.
Traders said the $3.50 mark in December was a key.
"There is a lot of selling at $3.50 in December," Bruce said.
That level was viewed as key technical resistance and also a psychological resistance point. The session high for December was $3.50-3/4.
"Everybody is trying to pick tops to sell right now but overall the market acts pretty well," said Paul Haugens, vice president for FIMAT Futures.
Corn closed two to six cents per bushel lower, with September down two at $3.67-3/4. December was down six at $3.42-3/4.
Nearby September was firm relative to other months on adjustment of the spreads. September was hit hard early this week as cash basis markets slid amid early harvesting of corn in the U.S. South.

Commercial bull spreading also boosted September relative to other months. Cargill Inc and Farmers Commodities Corp each bull spread three million bushels of September/December, traders said. Cargill Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of December, Iowa Grain sold two million December and FIMAT Futures sold 1.5 million December, the traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 42,000 contracts, down from 45,115 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options there was not one key feature, they said. "There were a lot of 100 and 200 lot trades with continued net premium buying," a trader said. "Volatility held steady in the December and firm in the March."
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, up from 12,578 Tuesday.
